newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota Atty Gen says opposes utility merger.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota Atty Gen says opposes utility merger.

text.p: Minnesota Attorney General Hubert Humphrey III said Friday he opposed a proposed merger between Northern States Power Co and Wisconsin Energy Corp, saying it could hamper competition.

"The last thing consumers need is fewer competitors just when we may be forced to depend on competition rather than regulation to protect us from monopoly prices," Humphrey said in a statement, referring to proposed deregulation of electricity prices.
He added the proposed merger "has the real potential to harm consumers and to hamper development of effective competition in the electric industry."
Dave Sparby, general manager of regulatory services of Northern States, said the utilities were disappointed v with the objections raised by the Minnesota Attorney General.
"The proposed transaction will result in a 1.5 percent reduction in electricity rates followed by a four-year freeze on rates," Sparby told Reuters.
Wisconsin Energy deferred comment to Northern States.
If the merger proceeds, the Wisconsin Energy/Northern States merger would create a utility with more than three million customers in five states and $6.0 billion in market capitalization.
The merged company would be called Primergy Corp.
The planned merger was first announced in May, 1995.
